title: Tangent surjectivity and underlying ring lifts characterize versality
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring and $k$ a field of finite type over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-field], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use the category $\mathcal C_{R,k}$ of Artinian local $R$-algebras with specified residue field $k$ and local maps inducing the identity on $k$ [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]. Let $\mathcal F$ be a predeformation category on $\mathcal C_{R,k}$ satisfying (RS), as defined in [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]. Let $C$ be a complete Noetherian local $R$-algebra with residue field $k$ and let $\xi$ be a formal object on $C$ [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]. Then $\xi$ is versal if the following two conditions hold. First the map $\operatorname{Hom}_{R,\mathrm{loc}}(C,k[\epsilon])\to T\mathcal F$, $a\mapsto[\xi_{k[\epsilon],a}]$, is surjective. Second, whenever $B\twoheadrightarrow A$ is a small extension, $a:C\to A$ is a local $R$-map inducing the identity on $k$, $y\in\mathcal F(B)$ and $y|_A\cong\xi_A$ is a specified isomorphism, there is a local $R$-map $b:C\to B$ lifting $a$ and inducing the identity on $k$; no isomorphism $y\cong\xi_B$ is assumed in this second condition. The conclusion supplies that isomorphism extending the specified one and applies to every surjection, as in the definition of versality.

source.place: Tag 06IU (lemma-versal-criterion), sufficient direction; (RS) implies both (S1) and (S2) by Tag 06J7 (lemma-RS-implies-S1-S2).

proof.text: It suffices to solve a small-extension lifting problem and then compose solutions. Indeed, [lem-sfb-artin-local-test-algebra] factors any surjection $B\to A$ into finitely many small extensions followed by an isomorphism. Transport along that final isomorphism first; for nonzero kernel the lemma also permits taking the final isomorphism to be the identity. Starting at the given map $C\to A$ and the given isomorphism, restrict $y$ to each intermediate quotient, and solve these problems successively. At each stage use the previously obtained isomorphism as the prescribed isomorphism for the next stage. The composite isomorphism at the end restricts to the originally specified one. For an isomorphism (zero small-extension factors), transport the given map and object along its inverse. Fix now a small extension $f:B\twoheadrightarrow A$, a map $a:C\to A$, and $\alpha:y|_A\cong\xi_a$. Hypothesis two supplies a ring lift $b:C\to B$. Put $y'=\xi_b$ and $I=\ker f$.

source.place: Tag 06IU (lemma-versal-criterion), sufficient direction; use the assumed (RS) equivalences directly in place of (S1), (S2), and Tag 06IT.

proof.text: Form $P=B\times_A B$, an object of the test category by [lem-sfb-artin-local-test-algebra], and write $p_1,p_2:P\to B$. The pair $(y',y,\alpha^{-1})$ with its specified identification over $A$ is an object of the fibre-product groupoid in the definition of (RS). Essential surjectivity of that equivalence gives $z\in\mathcal F(P)$ and isomorphisms $p_{1,*}z\cong y'$, $p_{2,*}z\cong y$ whose identification over $A$ is exactly $\alpha$. This retains the prescribed identification, rather than merely giving equality of unmarked isomorphism classes.

source.place: Tag 06IU (lemma-versal-criterion), sufficient direction; use the assumed (RS) equivalences directly in place of (S1), (S2), and Tag 06IT.

proof.text: Define $g:P\to k[I]$ by $g(u,v)=(\bar u,v-u)$. It is an $R$-algebra map: $v-u\in I$, $I^2=0$, and multiplication by any $u\in B$ on $I$ is multiplication by $\bar u$, since $\mathfrak m_B I=0$. The map $(p_1,g):P\to B\times_k k[I]$ is an isomorphism, with inverse $(u,(\bar u,t))\mapsto(u,u+t)$. Put $\theta=g_*z$. Choose a $k$-linear isomorphism $I\cong k$ (the kernel of a small extension is one-dimensional). It identifies $k[I]$ with $k[\epsilon]$ as $R$-algebras. Tangent surjectivity therefore gives a local residue-preserving $i:C\to k[I]$ and an isomorphism $\tau:\xi_i\cong\theta$. The unique arrows in $\mathcal F(k)$ ensure that this isomorphism respects the residue identifications.

source.place: Tag 06IU (lemma-versal-criterion), sufficient direction; use the assumed (RS) equivalences directly in place of (S1), (S2), and Tag 06IT.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-artin-local-test-algebra], the maximal ideals of $B$ and $k[I]$ are nilpotent. As $b$ and $i$ are local, choose $n\geq1$ such that both kill $\mathfrak m_C^n$. Write $D=C/\mathfrak m_C^n$, $h:D\to B$ and $j:D\to k[I]$ for their factorizations, and $x_1=\xi_n$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local] with $K=\mathfrak m_C^n$ to see that $D$ is Artinian local; its residue field is $k$ since $\mathfrak m_C^n\subseteq\mathfrak m_C$. Its formal-object value is $x_1$ by definition. Put $Q=D\times_A B$, using $fh:D\to A$. It is a test algebra. The map $q:Q\to P$, $(u,v)\mapsto(h(u),v)$, has first projection $h$ after $Q\to D$. Apply (RS) to $D\to B\leftarrow P$ (the map $p_1:P\to B$ is surjective). Since $D\times_B P=Q$, the pair $(x_1,z)$ with the isomorphism $h_*x_1\cong y'\cong p_{1,*}z$ gives $w\in\mathcal F(Q)$ with compatible identifications $w|_D\cong x_1$ and $q_*w\cong z$.

source.place: Tag 06IU (lemma-versal-criterion), sufficient direction; use the assumed (RS) equivalences directly in place of (S1), (S2), and Tag 06IT.

proof.text: Let $g_1=gq:Q\to k[I]$, so $g_1(u,v)=(\bar u,v-h(u))$. The same multiplication calculation gives an isomorphism $(\operatorname{pr}_D,g_1):Q\cong D\times_k k[I]$, with inverse $(u,(\bar u,t))\mapsto(u,h(u)+t)$. The pair $(\mathrm{id}_D,j)$ thus defines a local residue-preserving $R$-map $s:D\to Q$, a section of $\operatorname{pr}_D$, with $g_1s=j$. Under the (RS) equivalence for $D\times_k k[I]$, the object $s_*x_1$ has components $(x_1,j_*x_1)$ and $w$ has components $(x_1,\theta)$. Their component isomorphisms $\mathrm{id}_{x_1}$ and $\tau:j_*x_1\cong\theta$ form a morphism of triples, since $\mathcal F(k)$ has a unique arrow between any two objects. Full faithfulness of (RS) gives an isomorphism $s_*x_1\cong w$ whose component over $D$ is precisely that identity. Push this isomorphism to the second $B$ factor of $Q$. It identifies $\xi_{b'}$ with $y$, where $b'=\operatorname{pr}_B\circ s\circ(C\to D)$. Since $f\operatorname{pr}_B=fh\operatorname{pr}_D$ and $\operatorname{pr}_Ds=\mathrm{id}$, $fb'=a$. Compatibility of $w$ with $z$, and the identity component over $D$, say that the resulting isomorphism $y\cong\xi_{b'}$ restricts to exactly $\alpha$. This solves the small-extension problem; step 1 yields versality for every surjection.

lean.statement: theorem isVersal_of_tangent_surjective_of_ring_lifts {R k : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [Field k] [Algebra R k] [Algebra.FiniteType R k] (F : CofibredGroupoids.{u, v, w} R k) (hpre : IsPredeformation F) (hRS : IsRimSchlessinger F) (C : CompleteLocalAlgebra R k) (ξ : FormalObject F C) (htangent : Function.Surjective (fun a : LocalMap C (squareZeroTest (R := R) (k := k) k) ↦ (Quotient.mk _ (evaluate ξ a) : tangentSet F))) (hring : ∀ (A B : TestCategory R k) (f : B ⟶ A), IsSmallExtension f → ∀ (a : LocalMap C A) (y : fibre F B) (_α : (push F f).obj y ≅ evaluate ξ a), ∃ b : LocalMap C B, (map f).comp b.hom = a.hom) : IsVersal ξ
